governance.note: pjm-74 recipe verbatim (Manual-15 CC econ_low 1.00 / CT econ_high 1.27 offer moves, CAMPD historic unit-outage windows, measured monthly delivered gas + PJM zonal basis, coal PRB/BIT passthrough sigmoids with BIT floor 0.65, per-plant CAMPD must-run/committed tranches, retiree CEMS availability envelope, measured EIA-930 monthly hydro + 2024 backfill, EIA-860 BTM + 2024 backfill, priced interchange at measured reference-bus prices with per-seam p90 tie caps, energy+reserve co-opt on the measured PJM reserve requirement, reliability floor, commitment=False) plus exactly two new levers, both measured and forward-native (rule #12 admissibility test applied to each): (1) CT_PEAKER net-load deployment drag — the ERCOT-keeper/CAISO-keeper mechanism (per-hour min-gen floor clip(0.01108*netGW - 0.9987, 0, 0.46) on non-peak CT tranches, gated to the evening ramp h[15,22)). Trigger = system net-load (a forecast year has a load forecast and a wind/solar build, hence a net-load; more VRE lowers it and the drag responds), magnitude = a physical min-gen commitment level regressed from measured CAMPD pure-play CT capacity factor on EIA-930 PJM net-load 2023-2025 (scripts/derive_pjm_ct_netload_drag.py; ramp-window Spearman rho 0.50/0.51/0.60, year-stable). PJM's CF-vs-net-load curve is two-regime, so the fit is the applied clipped-line functional form itself (hinge SSE on binned medians, 0.133 vs 0.176 for the unclipped ERCOT-recipe line) — a fit to the MEASURED CF-vs-net-load relationship, never to a model residual. Explicitly NOT ct_mustrun_per_plant / ct_deployment_overlay (actuals pins, no forward analogue). (2) CC demonstrated-peak cap — cc_capacity_reconcile mode=cap (scripts/derive_cc_capacity_reconcile.py --iso PJM --mode cap): 17 pure-play CC plants whose model nameplate exceeds their CAMPD demonstrated sustained max (p99.9 net MW pooled 2023-25) by >1.1x are capped AT the demonstrated peak (-2686 MW phantom top-band capacity). A capability/availability quantity that regenerates from rolling CEMS history — the opposite-direction twin of the ERCOT raise-only reconcile — corroborated independently by EIA-860 winter ratings (Key 774 vs 778, Camden 139 vs 145, Ontelaunee 590 vs 591). Cross-source feasibility guard drops candidates whose EIA-923 annual net generation is infeasible at the CAMPD peak (Hunterstown implied CF 1.17, Ironwood 1.06, Allegheny 3-4-5 1.27 — CEMS telemetry artifacts, rule #13 misalignment exception, documented). No unit pinned to observed CEMS generation; no adder/haircut applied to a price or volume residual; no input rescaled so model output lands on actuals; coefficients regenerate for a forward year from forward drivers.
governance.residuals_note: Predicted signs stated in the driver docstring before solving and confirmed in direction: CT up all years, CC down all years, coal up slightly, floored-hour prices soften. Magnitudes vs pjm-74: CC_REGULAR -7.9/-7.7/-7.5 TWh and CT_PEAKER +4.0/+4.3/+4.5 TWh (2023/24/25) — more year-uniform than the floor-energy differentiation (4.7/6.3/7.2 TWh) implied, because the floor overlaps hours the LP already dispatched. The 2024 target gap closes substantially: CC_REGULAR +16.57 -> +8.84 TWh, CT_PEAKER -8.76 -> -4.48 TWh. Costs, accepted per rule #1/#11 (structurally-correct measured mechanisms are not reverted because a residual moved): 2023 CC -6.71 -> -14.56 TWh (the cap removes phantom capacity the 2023 fit was leaning on; root cause of the 2023 CC under-run is elsewhere), 2025 CT +6.66 -> +11.21 TWh (an over-run that pre-existed the floor; the floor adds ~4.5 on top — the 2025 CT overshoot axis is the offer/scarcity tail, out of scope pending the per-gen reserve thread docs/multi-iso/pjm-reserve-ordc.md). 2025 CC +0.33 -> -7.15. The remaining 2024 CC-over/CT-under residual and the 2023/2025 redistribution point at the missing commitment tightening / per-gen reserve structure (pjm-cc-overgen-recommendation Rank 1/2), not at the measured levers added here.
